title: Residential Electricity Supply Contract Expiration Notice Standard
content:
Regulatory compliance standard, Residential Electricity Supply. Every agreement with a fixed term receives two expiration notices: an initial renewal notice and a final options notice. Renewal notices are issued only on an active agreement with a fixed term, as shown by the agreement's status.

## Timing

- The **initial renewal notice** is compliant when its notice date falls no earlier than the plan's earliest initial-notice point and no later than its latest initial-notice point, both counted in calendar days before the contract end date.
- The **final options notice** is compliant when its notice date falls no later than the plan's latest final-notice point, in calendar days before the contract end date, and after the initial notice.

## Content and governing offer

Each notice states the plan offered for renewal, the renewal rate, and the month-to-month rate that applies in the first cycle after expiry if the customer makes no election. When the two notices state different offers, the final options notice governs.

## Delivery

Notices are delivered by email only to customers who enrolled through the web channel, and by mail otherwise.

## Compliance check (hypothetical agreement ending 2026-03-31, using the 60, 45 and 30-day points every plan carries)

| Notice | Notice date | Window | Compliant |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial renewal notice | 2026-01-30 | 60 days before, the earliest point | yes |
| Initial renewal notice | 2026-02-14 | 45 days before, the latest point | yes |
| Initial renewal notice | 2026-01-29 | 61 days before, too early | no |
| Initial renewal notice | 2026-02-15 | 44 days before, too late | no |
| Final options notice, initial notice dated 2026-02-10 | 2026-03-01 | 30 days before and after the initial notice | yes |
| Final options notice, initial notice dated 2026-02-10 | 2026-03-02 | 29 days before, too late | no |
